To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
emulsions containing a mixture of sitosterol and oryzanol can be gelled if the water activity of the emulsion is low and the oil phase is less polar.
the water-in-oil gelation capability of a β-sitosteroland γ-oryzanal mixture can be promoted by using oils of lower polarity and by reducing the wateractivity.
the formation of tubular microstructures in the oil phase of water-in-oil mixtures can be promoted by decreasing the water activity or by using less polar oils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of a new type of organogel, namely, a water-in-oil organogel.

the preparation of water-in-oil organogel emulsions with mixtues of β-sitostero and γ-oryzanols, and the influence of the water activity and type oil phase on the gelation capability of the emulsions.

the development of new emulsions that are stable and firm over time, even when the water content is relatively high, and which can be used as a food ingredient or as a delivery vehicle for active molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emulsions with a mixture of oryzanol/sitosterol and low water activity and low polar oil phase have a potential as a new generation of food emulsion-gel.
the formation of the oryzanol and β-sitosterols tubular microstructure can be promoted by lowering the water activity and by using oils of lower polarity.
the formation of sitostanol and γ-oryzanol tubular microstructures in the emulsion was promoted by reducing the salt concentration in the water phase or by using oils with lower polarity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the water-in-oil organogel emulsion can be produced by using a mixture of oryzanol/sitosterol and a suitable combination of oil and water phase.
the gelling capability of β-sitosteryl β-D-glucoside is dependent on both the oil and water phases of the emulsion.
the emulsions prepared from water containing salt and a mixture of β- sitosterol and γ-or yzanol in a low polar oil phase are promising as a new type of food product with a long shelf-life.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emulsion-gels can be used for a wide range of food products, such as dressings, sauces, or spreads.
the gelling capability of oryzanol can be enhanced by the presence of β-sitostrol in an emulsion.
the emulsion system is a very versatile system that can be used for preparing organogel-emulsified foods.
